problems: Only kingdom-of-mercia was touched (verdict fail); kingdom-of-lindsey (thin) is unchanged. Fix 7 (dissolve region without Oxford) was applied by the reviewer and checked, so fixes_applied counts the other 7 of 8.

Direction of vassal events is mixed across eu-11 dossiers: the schema says counterpart is the vassal itself, but the Kent, Essex and East Anglia dossiers record their own subordination with the overlord as counterpart, and the reviewer asked for Mercia's own client status under Wessex (879-918) with counterpart kingdom-of-wessex. Mercia now has both directions with the same counterpart string (Wessex a vassal 726-752 and 786-802, Mercia the client 879-918); the notes of each event say which, and the region tells (the client's own land). The compile step must read each relation once, from the overlord's file, or by region.

Mercia starts 527 while anglo-saxon-england dissolves 533 with no Mercia split: the land is claimed twice 527-533; the predecessor link is now in Mercia's identity; the split belongs to the anglo-saxon-england owner.

Ten pages were opened for the repairs (Offa, Coenwulf, Kingdom of Kent, Wihtred of Kent, Kingdom of East Anglia, Mercia, Wulfhere, Kingdom of Sussex, Wihtwara, Mercian Supremacy) against the original budget of nine, at the reviewer's instruction.

Meon valley region reuses the Sussex dossier's spec (Cliopatria Sussex 490 minus the county of Sussex) because the gazetteer has no Meon name; counterpart 'nobody' for the Meonware (no page names a Meonware king). Neither the 661 gain nor the loss changes any keyframe, as Cliopatria's Mercia shape never held the valley.
